statement:
Let $L$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $C/L$ be smooth proper of genus $g\ge2$, and let $P,Q\in C(L)$ be distinct points with conjugate sections in the geometrically prime-to-$p$ arithmetic fundamental group. Let $\pi:D	o C$ be an 'etale Galois cover with constant deck group $G$, $p
mid |G|$, and let $P'\in D(L)$ lie over $P$. There is a unique $Q'\in D(L)$ above $Q$ with \[ T=[Q'-P']\in J_D(L)[p^\infty]. \] It is nonzero. If $|G|$ is odd, every $1
e\delta\in G$ satisfies $\delta T
e T$. For any homomorphism of abelian varieties $h:J_D	o B$ over $L$ with $B(L)[p]=0$, we have $h(T)=0$.

statement: In the situation of AC.1, assume $|G|>1$ is odd. Put $h_L(X)=\#J_X(L)$. If \[ p\nmid h_L(D)/h_L(C), \] then $P$ collides with no distinct point of $C(L)$, and hence with no point rational over any specified subfield of $L$. The quotient in this display is a positive integer. More generally the same conclusion holds for any prime-to-$p$ group $G$ containing a nontrivial odd-order element, provided that element acts freely on $D$ as it does for an \'etale cover.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: For a fixed $C/L$ and $P\in C(L)$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item There is a nontrivial constant odd-order prime-to-$p$ Galois $P$-split \'etale cover satisfying criterion (R). \item There is such a cover with cyclic group of odd prime order. \end{enumerate} The extension field $L$ need not be changed. Consequently nonabelian odd-order groups and noncyclic abelian groups cannot enlarge the set of $(C,P,L)$ reached by the whole-relative-class-number criterion L1.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: Let $C/L$ be as above, $q=\#L$, $P\in C(L)$, and let $a:J_C(L)\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a nontrivial finite abelian quotient of order prime to $p$. For a nontrivial character $\psi:A\to\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$ define \[ c_d(\psi)=\sum_{E\in\operatorname{Div}^{+}_d(C)(L)} \psi\bigl(a([E-dP])\bigr), \qquad \kappa=[K_C-(2g-2)P]. \] Here an effective divisor is a Galois-invariant effective geometric divisor; it need not be a sum of rational points. The corresponding $P$-split Lang cover has twisted polynomial \[ L_P(\psi,T)=\sum_{d=0}^{2g-2}c_d(\psi)T^d, \qquad c_{2g-2}(\psi)=q^{g-1}\psi(a(\kappa)). \] For $g-1\le d\le2g-2$ one has \[ c_d(\psi)=q^{d+1-g}\psi(a(\kappa)) c_{2g-2-d}(\psi^{-1}). \tag{AC.1} \] In particular, modulo any prime above $p$, \[ L_P(\psi,1)\equiv \sum_{d=0}^{g-1}c_d(\psi). \tag{AC.2} \] For genus two this is exactly $L_P(\psi,1)\equiv1+\sum_{R\in C(L)}\psi(a([R-P]))$.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: With $A$ as in AC.4 put \[ \Theta_{C,P,A}=\sum_{d=0}^{g-1} \sum_{E\in\operatorname{Div}^{+}_d(C)(L)}[a([E-dP])] \quad\hbox{in }\mathbf F_p[A]. \] The full $A$-cover satisfies criterion (R) if and only if \[ \bar\psi(\Theta_{C,P,A})\ne0 \quad\text{for every nontrivial } \bar\psi:A\to\overline{\mathbf F}_p^{\times}. \tag{AC.3} \] One can equivalently sum through $2g-2$ in the definition of $\Theta$. For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell$, with $\ell$ an odd prime different from $p$, \[ \frac{h_L(D)}{h_L(C)} =\prod_{i=1}^{\ell-1}L_P(\psi^i,1) =N_{\mathbf Q(\zeta_\ell)/\mathbf Q}L_P(\psi,1). \] If $p$ generates $(\mathbf Z/\ell)^\times$, failure of (R) is equivalent to all the coefficients of $\Theta$ in $\mathbf F_p[\mathbf Z/\ell]$ being equal.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: For the same fixed character $\psi$ and rational base points $P,P_0$, \[ L_{P_0}(\psi,T) =L_P\bigl(\psi,\psi(a([P-P_0]))T\bigr). \tag{AC.4} \] The associated covers differ by the constant torsor with arithmetic Frobenius value $a([P-P_0])$ (up to reversing all Frobenius conventions consistently). Thus changing the base point is not innocuous for (R). For a finite extension $L'/L$, the base change of a $P$-split Lang cover corresponds to $a\circ N_{L'/L}:J_C(L')\to A$ and remains $P$-split. If a fixed cover fails (R) over $L$, it fails over every extension $L'$. If it satisfies (R), it need not do so over every extension.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement:
Suppose $g=2$ and $\ell
e p$ is an odd prime for which $p$ is a primitive root. Put $V=J_C(L)/\ell J_C(L)$ and $N_b=\#\{R\in C(L):[R-P] mod\ell J_C(L)=b\}$. If $P$ collides with a distinct point, then \[ N_b\equiv N_0+1\pmod p \quad(0
e b\in V). 	ag{AC.5} \] If $|V|>\#C(L)$, this implies $N_0\equiv-1\pmod p$ and $N_b\equiv0\pmod p$ for $b
e0$. For one surjection $a:J_C(L)	woheadrightarrow\mathbf Z/\ell$, let $H=\ker a$, $N=\#C(L)$. If \[ N\ge2|H|, \qquad \ell>N, 	ag{AC.6} \] then its cover satisfies (R).
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: For any genus $g\ge2$, any finite quotient $A$ of $J_C(L)$, and $N=\#C(L)$, let $N_b$ count the Abel-image points in the $A$-cosets. The number of ordered distinct pairs in the same coset satisfies \[ \sum_b N_b(N_b-1) \le\frac{N^2}{|A|} +\frac{|A|-1}{|A|}(2g-2)^2q-N. \tag{AC.7} \] If the nonzero occupancies are multiples of $p$, the same quantity is at least $(p-1)(N-N_0)$. These two estimates alone give a contradiction only if their displayed numerical bounds conflict; $|A|>N$ by itself and the inequality $p>(2g-2)^2$ are not the full hypotheses of such a finite-field contradiction.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: The genus-two expression $1+\sum_{R\in C(L)}\psi([R-P])$ does not test relative $p$-divisibility in genus three, even for a prime cyclic cover with $p$ a primitive root. An explicit example is \[ C/\mathbf F_2:\quad y^2+y=x^7+x^3,\qquad P=\infty. \] There is a surjection $\chi:J_C(\mathbf F_2)\to\mathbf Z/3$ whose point-coset counts are $(3,1,1)$ and whose twisted polynomial is \[ L_P(\chi,T)=1+2T+3T^2+4T^3+4T^4. \] Its relative class number is $196$, while the point-only expression reduces to $1$ modulo $2$. This is a counterexample to exporting that numerical test; it is not a collision or a counterexample to A1.
status: Refuted: the point-only extension to genus three
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: Let $\overline C/\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ have genus at least two and let $S$ be a finite set of odd primes different from $p$. Suppose that for every connected cyclic \'etale cover of degree $\ell\in S$, its new Jacobian factor has positive geometric $p$-rank. There is a finite-field model $C/k$ with $P\in C(k)$ such that no cyclic $P$-split cover of degree in $S$ satisfies (R), over any finite extension of $k$.
status: Proved: a finite-prime obstruction for the rational method
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: Let $C/L$ be smooth proper of genus $g\ge2$ and not geometrically a separable double cover of a genus-one curve. Let $D\to C$ be a connected \'etale cyclic cover of odd degree $n>1$ prime to $p$, with constant group $\langle\sigma\rangle$ and $P'\in D(L)$ over $P\in C(L)$. Define the homomorphism over $L$ \[ A=\prod_{\ell\mid n}(1-\sigma^{n/\ell}):J_D\to J_D, \qquad P_n=\operatorname{im}(A), \] where the product is over distinct prime factors. If $p\nmid\#P_n(L)$, then $P$ has no collision. Equivalently, a collision forces $p\mid\#P_n(L)$ on every such cover. This proves L4 with all field and nontriviality hypotheses explicit.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: The nontrivial-cover existence assertion A3 has not been proved or refuted by AC.1--AC.11. In its precise reduced form, it asks whether for every $C/k$ of genus at least two over a finite field and every $P\in C(k)$ there are a finite extension $L/k$, an odd prime $\ell\ne p$ and a surjection $J_C(L)\to\mathbf Z/\ell$ such that all its nontrivial twisted values $L_P(\chi^i,1)$ are $p$-adic units. This is equivalent to the version allowing every nontrivial odd-order Galois group by AC.3.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: Fix any prime $p$, any genus $g\ge2$, and any finite set $S$ of odd primes different from $p$. There are a finite field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a smooth proper geometrically connected ordinary genus-$g$ curve $C/k$, and $P\in C(k)$, such that no $P$-split cyclic cover of degree in $S$ satisfies (R), over any finite extension $L/k$. By AC.3 the same holds for all odd-order Galois covers whose group has prime divisors only in $S$. In particular there is no bound depending only on $(p,g)$ for the least prime of a rational L1 witness, even if every $(C,P)$ eventually has some witness.
notes: Candidate statement; root assigns final A.* numbering.

statement: Let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic two, $C/k$ a genus-two curve, and $P\in C(k)$. Let $\ell$ be an odd prime with $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(2)=\ell-1$. Suppose that every geometric cyclic degree-$\ell$ \'etale cover has ordinary new Jacobian factor. Suppose further that, for some $d>0$, the action of arithmetic Frobenius $F^d$ on $J_C[\ell](\overline k)$ is scalar $2^j$, with $\gcd(j,\ell-1)=1$, and that every eigenvalue of $F$ on this space has exact order $d(\ell-1)$. Then no constant-deck cyclic degree-$\ell$ $P$-split cover satisfies (R) over any finite extension of $k$.

Every connected geometric cyclic \'etale cover of either prime degree has ordinary Prym. The same statements hold for the coefficientwise-square conjugate curve.
